channel.title: Lynn Group Media - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Lynn Group Media (hoganstand.com)

item.title: Clogher rue missed chances and second half fadeout
item.description: Clogher manager Steven McKenna was left to rue missed first half goal chances and a disappointing second half display as his side came up short against Ballymacelligott in the All-Ireland club JFC final.

item.title: 'I'm sure dad would be very proud looking down'
item.description: Pádraig Ó Sé became the latest member of the famous Kerry football dynasty to win an All-Ireland medal at Croke Park yesterday.

item.title: 'Kerry are a good bit ahead of the chasing teams'
item.description: Brendan Devenney says Kerry are heading into the new season as favourites to retain their All-Ireland SFC crown.

item.title: Lyng happy to embrace Walsh Shield
item.description: Derek Lyng doesn't think Kilkenny are any worse off for playing in the Walsh Shield rather than the Walsh Cup as they gear up for the start of the Allianz Hurling League.

item.title: McGuinness disappointed to lose McBrearty
item.description: Jim McGuinness has paid tribute to Paddy McBrearty after the Kilcar forward was forced to retire from inter-county football on medical grounds.

item.title: Westmeath school seeks rare Leinster double
item.description: A Westmeath school has been gripped by hurling and football fever as it closes in on a rare Leinster double.

item.title: Critchley and O'Brien confirmed as Portlaoise bosses
item.description: Portlaoise have appointed Pat Critchley as their new senior hurling manager.

item.title: 'We're looking forward to a big year from Tony'
item.description: Jack O'Connor was suitably impressed by Tony Brosnan's scoring heroics against Waterford in the McGrath Cup last Sunday.

item.title: LGFA announce winners of 2025 National Volunteer of the Year awards
item.description: The Ladies Gaelic Football Association is pleased to announce the 2025 LGFA Volunteer of the Year award winners.

item.title: Tyrone expect to have McElholm and Canavan for start of the League
item.description: Tyrone boss Malachy O'Rourke is optimistic about Eoin McElholm and Darragh Canavan's chances of being fit for the start of the Allianz Football League against Kildare on Saturday week.
